newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals steady to higher in local markets.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals steady to higher in local markets.

text.p: Indian copper, aluminium and tin prices on Friday rose in local markets, dealers said.
Other base metals were steady amid narrow price range.
"Copper, aluminium and tin prices lifted further on the back of negligible arrivals of imported metals as well as shortage of ready stock which prompted speculative interest," a dealer said.

Physical buying however remained at a low ebb and trading volumes were dull. Copper rose by 50 rupees at 13,500 rupees per quintal while aluminium moved up by 25 rupees at 7,425 rupees per quintal. Tin lifted by 100 rupees at 37,600 rupees per quintal.

Nickel was steady at 37,300 rupees per quintal, zinc at 7,700 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal amid limited activity but sentiments was firm following poor arrivals, said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
The Bombay metal markets are closed on Monday for the Holi festival (festival of colours).
